en.title: Longest Tree Path with Different Adjacent Characters
en.description:
A tree is rooted at 0, and each node carries a lowercase letter. Return the maximum number of nodes on any simple path in which every pair of adjacent nodes has different characters.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, examples, solution, and tests.
en.input: This site's ranges: the first line contains N (1..100000), the second line contains N parent values (parent[0]=−1; the others are 0-based parent indices), and the third line contains N lowercase letters. The input is guaranteed to be a valid tree.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation:
Example 1: 0—1—3 has distinct characters a, b, c, so the longest path has 3 nodes.

Example 2: 2—0—3 with b, a, c forms a path of length 3.

Example 3: there is only one node, so the answer is 1.
hints: Compute bottom-up the longest valid downward chain from each node, and update the answer with the two longest child chains that can be connected through it.
